title: Ontario municipal systems that convert housing targets into completed units
question: Which municipal systems can convert housing targets into completed units?
why_it_matters: Provincial targets and housing demand matter only if municipal planning, servicing, approvals, infrastructure, labor, and financing can convert them into occupied homes.
current_support: FTFN has Ontario housing supply progress, CMHC and Statistics Canada data, a June 2026 CMHC stage baseline for approved-but-not-started units, active construction, completions, and starts in the Toronto CMA, and Toronto application 24 254930 from notice through staff review, committee recommendation, and City Council adoption without amendments on July 29-30, 2026. The Council record retains explicit bill-withholding conditions. Toronto's 2025 Development Pipeline, Toronto Water's adopted 2026-2035 capital plan, IESO's 2026 electricity outlook, and Toronto Hydro's OEB distribution proceeding remain system context.
missing_evidence: final servicing conditions and detailed design
introduced and enacted by-laws for application 24 254930
satisfaction of the wind-study, land-exchange, and laneway conditions
project-specific infrastructure funding and utility connections
stage conversion and completions by municipality
candidate_records: Toronto application 24 254930 City Council decision and enacted by-laws
next_action: Use the current CMHC stage baseline as aggregate context only. Recheck application 24 254930 on September 9 for introduced or enacted amendment numbers and accepted wind, land-exchange, laneway, or servicing conditions, then track a confirmed building permit, financing, start, completion, and occupancy.

named_records: Toronto City Council item 2026.SC33.9 for application 24 254930
latest_review.stage_result: The Council gate is closed: Toronto adopted item 2026.SC33.9 without amendments. The gap narrows to enactment and delivery because the amendment bills remain withheld behind named wind, land-exchange, and laneway conditions.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not treat metropolitan stocks and flows as a same-project conversion rate, and do not treat Council adoption as enactment, servicing, a permit, start, completion, or occupancy.

notes: Phase 61 reconciles the completed Council decision and removes the past-due watch language. Citywide and CMA measures still do not prove enacted by-laws, condition compliance, project utility connections, a building permit, financing, construction, completion, or occupancy.
